newsitem.title: FRANCE: French unions call transport strike for January 24.
newsitem.headline: French unions call transport strike for January 24.

text.p: Six French trade unions on Thursday called a nationwide 24-hour strike in the public transport sector for January 24 to press demands for early retirement and a cut in working hours.
The unions, including the country's three biggest -- the CFDT, CGT and Force Ouvriere -- said in a statement that the decision was taken at a joint meeting on Tuesday.

"(We) note a strong determination to act in favour of retirement at 55 years, work rule reforms and a significant cut in the working week to 35, or even 32 hours without any loss in wages, which will create stable jobs," the statement said.
Strikes on similar demands hit the public transport sector in several French cities in November and December.
The government late last year yielded to truckers who set up roadblocks on highways across the country to press demands for retirement at 55 instead of 60, and for cuts in working hours.
